shapes.html: We define system composition through single-step components.

notes: We have three basic forms. Sequential composition feeds one component output into the next. Pass-through carries another signal alongside a component. Parallel composition places two branches alongside each other. Each component shown here carries its own state. We want to describe these constructions at the single-step level while preserving their behaviour over logical time. Use the pointer/oral progression without extra clicks. Connect pass-through to P9 synchronous pairing; explain the visible orientation (the other is developed on P17). Parallel composition here is not physical scheduling or processor placement. Distinct state resources remain distinct; ordinary composition does not arbitrarily share one state resource. Precise types appear on P17. Transition: We can also view each of these networks as one composite stateful component.

source.html: The function run lifts single-step behaviour to a sequence of reactions.
With one input consumed per iteration, the lifting gives the Mealy-machine behaviour of f and initial state st.
We can define composition through single-step components and justify its behaviour through run.
